sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Home Hydroponics and Gardening Equipment

stage_1.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
stage_1.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (protocolized original) or the Founder's Notary abroad in the case of foreign incorporation documents
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for origin documents from Hague Convention member states) OR Consular Legalization (for non-member states)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Ley N° 21 de 2017; Articles 1–10 (constitution, name, registered office), 13–17 (registration and public filing), and 25–29 (Foundation Council and supervision).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Foundation Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter Deed), notarized by a Panamanian Notary Public and registered in the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital is legally imposed; the Foundation Charter must state an initial patrimony, with a nominal standard of US$10,000 customarily used. There is no escrow account requirement; the endowment remains at the founder's direction subject to the foundation's objects.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Private Interest Foundation is formally constituted under Law 25 of 1995. The initial patrimony declared in the foundation deed is accepted and recorded. The registered office at the address stated in Article 4 of the charter is adopted as the foundation's legal seat. The following persons are hereby appointed to the Foundation Council: [Founder/Patron] as President, [Secretary] as Secretary, and [Treasurer] as Treasurer, each to serve for a one-year term or until substituted. The appointees accept office and are authorized to open bank accounts, sign mandates, and execute all acts within the foundation's objects in Panama and abroad.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Department of Name Certification (Certificado de Nombre).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online or in-person application for a name certificate indicating the proposed foundation name ending with 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'P.I.F.' The certificate is valid for 30 days, during which the charter must be notarized and presented for registration.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed through a resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, submit up to two alternates and request reconsideration under Registro Público procedure; no additional governmental charge applies for the first alternate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito in Panama (any licensed Panamanian notary).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado, including the foundation name, initial patrimony, registered office, council members or founder reservation, objects (including e-commerce of hydroponics/gardening equipment), and duration, then execute before the notary with the founder or authorized agent.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or ID of founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary may require correction if any statutory clause is inconsistent with Ley 25; the instrument is re-executed on the same day, and an apostilled/certified copy can be issued if the charter is to be used abroad.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Deed in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized deed and the name certificate to the Registry; pay the statutory inscription arancel, and obtain the registered 'copia inscrita' (foundation existence certificate) with an assigned registration number and date.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial protocol
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an 'advertencia' (observation), rectify the indicated clause by private amendment or new notarial document, pay the current fee, and resubmit; Registry officers usually process the correction within two working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of resident agent and registered office confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent firms (e.g., law firms/trust companies) and the Public Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the resident agent acceptance agreement and file the corresponding notice with the Registry; register the physical local address as the foundation's legal office for service of process.
required_dossiers: Proof of local address for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent's license is suspended, a replacement licensed agent must be designated within the statutory calendar period; the Registry will accept substitution via a notarized private document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and banking activation for territorial-scope e-commerce operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; local banks / AML compliance units.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although the foundation is not engaged in Panamanian-source income, open a corporate bank account with a licensed bank, complete client due diligence, and, if the foundation later receives Panama-source income, register with DGI to obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) and obtain a notice of operations for the commercial activity, if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or DGI queries the file, provide the certified foundation documents and a legal opinion from the resident agent clarifying the PIF's legal structure and source of funds; resubmit the corrected KYC package within the authority's response window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial or manufacturing activity is conducted in Panama; the activity is online retail / e-commerce resale.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no commercial operating license is required for pure online sales of home hydroponics equipment under Panamanian municipal licensing rules (Aviso de Operación may be required if a physical local store is opened).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The operation generates no industrial wastewater, air emissions, VOC discharge, or hazardous waste. If warehousing is conducted, standard solid-waste handling must comply with municipal collection regulations and Regulation DGNTI-COPANIT 14-2000 for non-hazardous waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for pure e-commerce and virtual business activities. If an administrative office is leased, the premises must hold a municipal occupancy permit, fire-safety inspection certificate (Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá), and basic electrical and structural compliance as required by local law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official e-services portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (SIE – Sistema de Facturación Electrónica and RUC module)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign settlor or resident agent must (1) register the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) with the Registro Público de Panamá under Ley 25 de 1995; (2) obtain the Aviso de Operación (business notice) and RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) via the DGI portal, submitting the foundation charter, Registered Agent license proof, copy of identity documents, and the Aviso de Operación issued by the municipality; (3) activate the DGI e-Tax account and obtain the fiscal digital certificate for electronic invoicing. No local residency or economic substance is required for the PIF, but the local Registered Agent is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style pass-through election exists under Panamanian law. The PIF is a hybrid legal person: settlor retains control unless the charter provides otherwise, and assets/income are segregated from the founder's patrimony. For CRS/FATCA classification the PIF may elect its status as a passive NFE or investment entity, affecting reporting only, not taxation. The foundation charter (Pacto Constitutivo) can elect the distribution mechanism (interest/participation) and the governing law, but territorial taxation applies regardless. No hybrid mismatch election is available under Panama's domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – consumption tax of the VAT type
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0 – no ITBMS registration threshold; any person habitually engaged in taxable commerce inside Panama must register for RUC and ITBMS. A small taxpayer simplified regime applies for annual gross turnover up to B/.36,000, where a fixed quarterly quota replaces the 7% general rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide e-invoicing per Law 75 de 2019 and DGI Resolution 230-3446 de 2019. The PIF must issue XML e-invoices through the DGI'SIE platform or an authorized Electronic Invoicing Service Provider. Each invoice receives a real-time DGI digital acknowledgment and a validation code (Código de Verificación) for the transaction; the customs module cross-references export declarations. Full API integration is required for marketplaces/payment rails, including Stripe and PayPal. The SIE is also used for issuing zero-rated export invoices and the 'Comprobante de Exportación'.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including B2C online retail shipments of hydroponics and gardening equipment sold by the Panamanian PIF to foreign buyers) qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when title passes to a non-resident and the goods physically leave the Panamanian customs territory. Sales of services rendered to non-residents for use entirely abroad are also zero-rated. The PIF must maintain evidence that proceeds derive from foreign buyers and that the goods left Panama within the statutory export window; e-commerce marketplaces (Stripe/PayPal) settlement records must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) submitted via SIGA/VUPA portal, referencing the SIE export invoice
Commercial invoice issued through SIE with 0% ITBMS and the export validation code
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Panamanian territory
Inward remittance certificate or payment settlement report from the payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) confirming funds received from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI cross-validates SIE e-invoices against the customs SIGA/VUPA database; unjustified zero-rating triggers retroactive ITBMS assessment at 7% plus monthly 10% late-payment recargo (Código Fiscal), fines ranging from 10% to 300% of the evaded tax, and clawback of any input tax credits claimed. False export documentation constitutes fiscal and customs fraud under Ley 45 de 2023, carrying criminal penalties and joint liability of the Registered Agent and PIF directors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a traditional central bank or domestic currency-issuing authority. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the prudential regulator with oversight of banking and foreign-exchange operations; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the fiscal agent of the State; and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) coordinates financial policy. The monetary system is fully dollarized: the US dollar is legal tender and the Balboa (PAB) circulates only as coins at a fixed 1:1 parity, so de facto monetary conditions are anchored by the monetary policy of the US Federal Reserve.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama applies full convertibility on both current account and capital account. There is no central-bank authorization, no investment-registration gate, and no surrender or repatriation permission required for capital injections, profits, dividends, or Private Interest Foundation (PIF) distributions; the only practical compliance gates are AML/CFT documentation and FATF travel-rule data on wire transfers. Under territorial taxation, Panama-source income earned by a local operating e-commerce entity is taxable in Panama (25% corporate income tax, 7% ITBMS value-added tax where applicable, and 10% dividend withholding on distributions of taxed Panama-source profits), while foreign-source income held or earned through the PIF is exempt. Non-resident beneficiaries receiving PIF distributions from foreign-source assets carry no Panama tax liability, and USD/PAB conversion is absolute at 1:1 with no remittance hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no statutory timeframe for repatriating export receipts. The PIF and its trading subsidiary may lawfully retain 100% of export and e-commerce proceeds in USD, or convert and hold them in any designated bank inside or outside Panama. For AML and audit defense, the commercial trail (commercial invoices, packing lists, Panamanian customs export declarations, and payment-processor settlement statements) should be retained for at least five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency USD base) and e-commerce settlement account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with UCP600 documentary credit services
Operational Account with merchant-acquiring support for card-not-present e-commerce flows
Capital Escrow Account and private-banking account for the PIF structure
Operational Account and treasury line for trade finance and FX hedging
Operational Account (state-owned fiscal agent; conservative mandate)
Operational Account (retail and correspondent banking focus)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium overall viability with a mandatory structural workaround for Stripe. PayPal fully supports Panama-domiciled business accounts and serves as the primary local e-commerce payment rail. Stripe does not support direct onboarding of a Panama-domiciled entity, so the PIF must establish a foreign-incorporated SPV (for example, a Delaware LLC incorporated through Stripe Atlas or local counsel) to hold the Stripe merchant account, with SPV profits distributed to the PIF via a documented capital and distribution trail. Offshore EMIs (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, Mercury) are viable as complementary collection and vendor-payout rails, but Panamanian Tier-1 banks treat EMI inflows as heightened-risk and require underlying transaction evidence; some EMIs internally decline private-interest foundations. The SBP Fintech Hub sandbox does not yet provide a practical full EMI license for this business model; the recommended architecture is PayPal Panama plus Stripe through a US SPV plus a Tier-1 Panamanian USD master clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Effectively mandatory in person for first activation. Law 23 of 2015 and SBP customer-due-diligence regulations oblige banks to identify the client through a direct interview; Tier-1 banks require at least one natural-person signatory, either the foundation council president or an attorney-in-fact resident in Panama, to appear physically at the bank's compliance office in Panama City for original-signature verification and the know-your-client interview. Remote video onboarding is accepted only by a minority of banks (notably Towerbank and Global Bank) and only when the entire corporate package is apostilled and introduced by a licensed Panamanian registered agent, with the electronic KYC file completed in advance; it never waives the statutory identification duty. One in-person director visit should be budgeted to activate the accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation (PIF) ownership opacity: nominee-protected structure triggers beneficial-ownership red flags under Law 23 of 2015 and the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales requirements of Ley 129 de 2020.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the registered foundation deed (acta fundacional) from the Registro Público; current Final Beneficial Owners Registry certificate; notarized organizational chart showing founder, council, protector, and beneficiaries; licensed Panamanian registered-agent reference letter; sworn source-of-funds declaration; and authenticated passports with tax-residency evidence of all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hydroponics and grow-equipment merchandise flagged as cannabis-cultivation paraphernalia, creating reputational and counter-financing-of-terrorism risk despite the Low_Risk_Standard tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SKU-level product catalog and supplier invoices; marketing evidence proving indoor household gardening and controlled-environment hobby use; HS classification memorandum (for example, HS 8414 for fans, HS 9405 for lighting) prepared by a customs broker; written certification that no products are sold under Panama's medical-cannabis framework (Ley 242 de 2021); and an external compliance opinion confirming the exclusion of scheduled substances and drug-related accessories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce chargeback and refund volatility (PayPal and Stripe settlement risk) undermining income-trail integrity and liquidity forecasting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six to twelve months of payment-processor settlement statements; a chargeback and dispute register with disposition details; a published refund and return policy; documented chargeback ratios below the 0.65% Visa and 0.90% Mastercard warning thresholds; and a proposed bank-reserve or merchant-escrow structure to absorb settlement volatility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No operating history and absence of tax registration for the foundation or its trading subsidiary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) certificate from the Dirección General de Ingresos; municipal aviso de operación; opening financial statements of the operating company; platform store reports from Shopify or Amazon evidencing active sales; and a corporate resolution authorizing account opening with designated signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote-signatory structure with power-of-attorney triggers impersonation and fraud controls, plus heightened scrutiny of foundation distributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled powers of attorney; certified passport copies of each attorney-in-fact; independent verification by the registered agent; a live videoconference with the bank's compliance officer; and a written undertaking to notify the bank of SBP-reportable changes within the statutory period (generally 30 days).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from founders or external investors should be executed by SWIFT MT103 in USD with the remittance information (field 70) reading Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation or aporte de capital, and with complete FATF travel-rule fields: field 50K for the ordering customer, field 57A for the intermediary bank where applicable, and field 59 for the beneficiary with the foundation's exact legal name and account number. No SBP or central-bank approval is required for the transfer; the bank's KYC/AML committee will request the registered foundation deed showing the endowment capital, a council resolution authorizing receipt, RUC certificates, and source-of-funds statements for wires above enhanced due-diligence thresholds (commonly USD 100,000 or at account opening). E-commerce operating proceeds should flow through PayPal and Stripe settlement sweeps into the same USD master operating account to avoid third-party funnel-account patterns that trigger compliance red flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for hydroponic hardware are executed through: (a) SWIFT MT103 for single foreign supplier payments and MT101 batch files for periodic multi-vendor cycles; (b) UCP600-compliant sight letters of credit issued through Banistmo or BAC for bulk procurement from China and Taiwan, with the required document set (commercial invoice, full-set bills of lading, packing list, certificate of origin) strictly matching LC terms; (c) standby letters of credit under ISP98 for critical contract vendors; and (d) domestic ACH and Fedwire clearing through the bank's US correspondent network for US-based couriers and third-party logistics providers. All USD flows clear through the US banking system (Fedwire/CHIPS), so OFAC/SDN screening and Panamanian sanctions enforcement apply automatically. PayPal and Stripe processor floats should be swept daily to the Panamanian master account to concentrate liquidity and minimize counterparty exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR, USD/GBP, and USD/CHF outright foreign-exchange forwards with SBP-licensed Tier-1 banks for firm procurement commitments; no SBP authorization required.
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge Chinese supplier payables denominated in offshore renminbi, settled in USD without physical CNY delivery.
USD/EUR and USD/CNY foreign-exchange swaps for temporary liquidity redistribution between operating accounts and procurement pipelines.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/CNY) under an ISDA Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, subject to bank treasury credit approval, for long-term payable and receivable matching.

Limited European-style option structures (collars and floor-ceiling strategies) for e-commerce margin stabilization; speculative uncovered positions are restricted by SBP risk-management expectations and each bank's internal treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) applicable to Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment processed through the registered agent and remitted to the National Treasury
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year recurring obligation due by March 31 of each year; DGI permits installment payment of 50% by March 31, 25% by June 30, and 25% by September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus 1.5% monthly default interest under the Código Fiscal; continued arrears block issuance of tax clearance (paz y salvo) and certificates of good standing, suspend registration of documents at the Public Registry, and may lead to administrative strike-off or inactivation of the foundation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Declaration of Final Beneficiaries (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) – UBO annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually filed between January 1 and March 31 (hard deadline March 31); must be updated within 90 days of any change in the ultimate beneficial owners of the foundation's assets or economic rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DGI-imposed fines for untimely or inaccurate filings; non-compliant foundations may be denied paz y salvo, good-standing certificates, and the capacity to inscribe documents, with escalating administrative penalties for persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) – contingent obligation only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the relevant fiscal year (calendar-year accounting) solely if the foundation derives Panamanian-source income or is inscribed as a merchant exercising industrial and commercial activities in Panama; otherwise no return is legally due under the territorial tax model
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For taxable foundations: 10% late-filing or underpayment surcharge plus 1.5% monthly interest; civil and administrative fines escalate for deliberate non-compliance, and DGI may initiate collection measures against any Panamanian assets of the foundation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on Private Interest Foundations by Law 25 of 1995; a mandatory independent audit may arise only if the foundation is registered as a merchant carrying on taxable commercial or industrial activity in Panama, or if its Foundation Charter and Regulations expressly require an annual audit. No capital or revenue threshold applies to a passive PIF; transparency obligations are satisfied through the confidential Beneficiaries and Assets Registers rather than audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (NIF) where the foundation has Panamanian taxable activity or voluntarily prepares financial statements; otherwise the Foundation Charter may designate internal bookkeeping standards, and the foundation is not required to publish financial statements. Books and records must accurately reflect the foundation's assets, liabilities, transfers, and beneficiary interests.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Foundations have no share capital or share transfers; changes in economic interest are effected through the Foundation Council and documented in Charter amendments or council resolutions designating or replacing beneficiaries. The registered agent and DGI require an annual sworn confirmation identifying all ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons holding more than 10% of economic rights or exercising control), due by March 31 and updated within 90 days of any change; the private Beneficiaries Register maintained at the registered office must be concurrently refreshed and made available for inspection by the competent anti-money-laundering supervisory authority upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Council Minute Book (actas del Consejo de Fundación)
Foundation Charter and Regulations (Escritura Pública) with all amendments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800 – 1,500 per year: standard registered agent, registered office, franchise tax processing, UBO declaration filing, and compliance administration fees for a Panama Private Interest Foundation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (not required for a non-commercial PIF); if voluntarily commissioned or triggered by Panamanian-source commercial activity, typical certified audit fee ranges from 2,500 – 6,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxable; foreign-source income is exempt. Reduced 5% dividend withholding rate applies when the distributing company/foundation's annual taxable income does not exceed B/. 1,100,000 (USD 1,100,000). Preferential deductions available for ordinary and necessary expenses incurred in generating Panama-source revenue; no entity-level tax on foreign e-commerce sales. PIFs remain subject to the 25% rate on Panama-source profits only.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 145 (Declaración Anual del Impuesto Sobre la Renta) filed electronically through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 portal using the taxpayer's RUC and digital certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before the last business day of March, unless extended to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and legal identification of the PIF.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF must obtain a RUC when deriving Panama-source income; non-resident founders and beneficiaries are not co-registrants and require no Panamanian tax ID.
State the exact annual period; PIFs may adopt the calendar year or a custom fiscal year as registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue subject to Panamanian territorial taxation (sales of goods delivered or used in Panama).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude all foreign-source online sales; only Panama-source e-commerce revenue is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses attributable to reported revenue (inventory, logistics, platform fees, resident agent fees, local overhead).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with invoices and accounting records maintained in Panama; cross-border related-party purchases require transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after application of prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply net operating loss carryforward, maximum 5 years, derived solely from previously declared Panama-source losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at 25% (Impuesto sobre la Renta).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No branch-level or remittance tax applies to the PIF itself at this line; withholding obligations on outbound distributions are separate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (anticipos) paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly installment Form 147 payments are credited; shortfall triggers statutory recargo and interest.
Settle via DGI-approved electronic channels; a zero-return annex is required for PIFs with no Panama-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of 5% of the tax due for the first month plus 1% for each subsequent month, capped at 25%; late payment: statutory recargo of 10% plus 1% monthly interest on unpaid tax; non-filing may trigger administrative fines on the legal representative and suspension of the RUC or foundation registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or distributions paid out of Panama-source profits; reduced to 5% where the distributing entity's annual taxable income does not exceed B/. 1,100,000 (USD 1,100,000).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Invoke a Panama double taxation agreement by obtaining a Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) from the recipient's treaty jurisdiction, apostilled or legalized as applicable, and submitting it with a DTA relief application to the DGI through E-Tax 2.0 before or at the time of payment. The payer must retain the approved documentation for at least five years. Panama's treaty network is limited (including South Korea, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, UAE, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, and Barbados); treaty dividend rates generally range 5-10%, subject to ownership thresholds and substance verification. Moroccan, UK, or other non-treaty jurisdictions are unprotected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis withholding of 12.5% applies to interest, royalties, and technical-service payments remitted to non-residents under the Fiscal Code remittance tax regime; treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 2-10% and royalties to 5-10% only upon successful TRC-based relief. Payments routed through shell entities without minimum economic substance are denied treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 3,000,000 (Balboa, pegged 1:1 to USD 3,000,000) of annual gross revenue: taxpayers at or above this threshold executing cross-border related-party transactions (e.g., purchase of hydroponics equipment from an affiliated supplier, management fees, or IP licensing) must prepare and file the Local File, Master File, and the annual transfer pricing informative return with the income tax return. Below-threshold taxpayers remain subject to the arm's length standard and must maintain contemporaneous records.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Requirements (Law 254 of 2021, effective fiscal year 2022) apply to all legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations, performing relevant activities. Online distribution of hydroponics and garden equipment constitutes a distribution and service center relevant activity, requiring: (i) annual sworn economic substance declaration filed with the DGI; (ii) core income-generating activities (management, procurement, inventory decisions) conducted in Panama; (iii) physical presence, local employees or outsourced arrangements with local substance, and complete accounting records maintained in Panama; (iv) adequate local expenditure proportional to income. A PIF lacking substance is presumptively a shell entity and may lose territorial tax treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of Panama-source revenue, inflation of fictitious deductions, or use of foreign invoices to disguise taxable e-commerce income (e.g., routing Panamanian sales through an offshore website company lacking substance).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion (Criminal Code Art. 277-A): imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; fines up to 10 times the tax evaded; retroactive reassessment of expired periods upon proof of fraud; civil liability for unpaid tax, recargo, and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, founder, and the resident agent who sign or cause the false return may be jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, penalties, and defense costs; criminal imprisonment and judicial travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a letterbox: no employees, no local management, no accounting records in Panama, and failure to file the annual sworn economic substance declaration under Law 254 of 2021 while deriving distribution income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to B/. 1,000,000; classification as a shell entity allowing the DGI/ULAF to disregard separate legal personality; cancellation of foundation registration; retroactive taxation of foreign-source income; inclusion on international blacklists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and the resident agent sustaining the shell structure face personal civil liability for tax assessments, closure orders, regulatory debarment, and potential money laundering charges with 5-12 years' imprisonment where funds disguise illicit origin.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing inventory from an affiliated foreign supplier above arm's length prices, or paying royalties or management fees to a related offshore entity to strip Panamanian profits, especially while avoiding the B/. 3,000,000 documentation threshold without benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of pricing with upward taxable income adjustment; penalty of 5% to 15% of the under-declared tax difference plus deficiency interest; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation triggers separate fines up to B/. 50,000 per omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Approving officers may be held jointly liable for the transfer pricing adjustment, fines, and, if intentional, tax evasion sanctions including personal bankruptcy, director disqualification, and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, failing to report foundation beneficiaries in the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales under Law 70 of 2019, or processing sales proceeds through Stripe/PayPal without source-of-funds documentation; using the PIF as an intermediate layer to evade reporting requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML fines under Law 23 of 2015 and UBO registry penalties up to B/. 50,000 per violation; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code Art. 254 carries 5-12 years' imprisonment and asset seizure; professional facilitators face aggravated penalties; jurisdiction-level FATF/EU grey-listing consequences may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, and the guardian (Protector) face personal criminal liability for money laundering of 5-12 years' imprisonment, fines, travel bans, asset freeze orders, disqualification from office, and civil restitution claims; professional advisors who fail to report suspicious transactions are also exposed.
